proposals.before: For generations they lived in the Liao marshes on the south bank of the Huang River. Yumen Pass lay eleven hundred li to their south, and Youzhou another seven hundred li beyond the pass — lands that had once belonged to the Xianbei.
proposals.after: For generations they lived in the Liao marshes on the south bank of the Huang River. Yuguan lay eleven hundred li to their south, and Youzhou another seven hundred li beyond the pass — lands that had once belonged to the Xianbei.
proposals.reason: 榆關 is Yuguan (the pass near Shanhaiguan), not Yumen Pass (玉門關) in the Hexi Corridor.

proposals.before: For generations they dwelt amid the Liao marshes, on the south bank of the Huang River; one thousand one hundred li south to Yumen Pass, and seven hundred li south from Yumen Pass to Youzhou — the old territory of the Xianbei.
proposals.after: For generations they dwelt amid the Liao marshes, on the south bank of the Huang River; one thousand one hundred li south to Yuguan, and seven hundred li south from Yuguan to Youzhou — the old territory of the Xianbei.
proposals.reason: 榆關 is Yuguan, not Yumen Pass (玉門關); the same mistranslation appears in the literal rendering.

proposals.before: Emperor Wenzong was heroic and martial; within a few years he captured both Turks and made them palace guards.
proposals.after: Emperor Wen was heroic and martial; within a few years he captured both Turks and made them palace guards.
proposals.reason: 文皇 is Tang Taizong's posthumous style 文皇帝, not Tang Wenzong (文宗). The idiomatic rendering already has Emperor Taizong.

proposals.before: The Chief Commander north of the river, Lord Ling — recently because of the Weizhou military mutiny the late emperor issued an edict ordering his punishment; once he heard of internal troubles, the army and masses lost heart, and when the capital had no lord, high and low firmly enthroned Lord Ling and asked him to preside over the altars of soil and grain — he has now followed the people's hope and ascended the imperial throne."
proposals.after: The Chief Commander north of the river, Lord Ling — recently because of the Weizhou military mutiny the late emperor issued an edict ordering him to suppress it; once he heard of internal troubles, the army and masses lost heart, and when the capital had no lord, high and low firmly enthroned Lord Ling and asked him to preside over the altars of soil and grain — he has now followed the people's hope and ascended the imperial throne."
proposals.reason: 除討 means to suppress the Weizhou mutiny, not to punish Lord Ling. The idiomatic rendering already has the correct sense.

proposals.before: At that time Zhao Dejun of Youzhou encamped at Tuanbai Valley, sent envoys to the tent headquarters, asked to be enthroned himself with the Shi clan hereditarily holding Taiyuan; Deguang answered the envoy, pointing at a stone before the tent: "I have already pledged brotherhood with Lord Stone — when stone rots it may change."
proposals.after: At that time Zhao Dejun of Youzhou encamped at Tuanbai Valley, sent envoys to the tent headquarters, asked to be enthroned himself with the Shi clan hereditarily holding Taiyuan; Deguang answered the envoy, pointing at a stone before the tent: "I have already pledged a father-and-son alliance with Lord Stone — when stone rots it may change."
proposals.reason: Chinese 父子之盟 is a father-son pact, not brotherhood. The idiomatic rendering already has the correct bond.

proposals.before: In Qingtai 3 the Jin founder was besieged by Zhang Jingda and others. He sent Commander He Fuben with a petition begging for Khitan aid and offering to become their vassal.
proposals.after: In Qingtai 3 the Jin founder was besieged by Zhang Jingda and others. He sent Commander He Fu with a petition begging for Khitan aid and offering to become their vassal.
proposals.reason: 何福賫表 is He Fu carrying a memorial (賫=to present); 賫 is not part of the personal name.

proposals.before: In the third month of year two he ordered Xuzhou military governor Wang Yanchao and others to build fortifications at Li Yankou. They fought several thousand Khitan horsemen at Anping county and defeated them.) 〉
proposals.after: In the third month of year two he ordered Xu-prefecture military governor Wang Yanchao and others to build fortifications at Li Yankou. They fought several thousand Khitan horsemen at Anping county and defeated them.) 〉
proposals.reason: 許州 is Xu prefecture (Xuchang), not 徐州 (Xuzhou). The same error is easy to miss in English.

decisions.reason: 榆關 is Yuguan near Shanhaiguan, not Yumen Pass in the Hexi Corridor.
The literal field repeats the same confusion of 榆關 with 玉門關; Yuguan is correct.

decisions.after: Emperor Taizong was heroic and martial; within a few years he captured both Turks and made them palace guards.
decisions.reason: 文皇 refers here to Tang Taizong, as the surrounding passage and idiomatic field establish. Emperor Taizong is clearer than the ambiguous posthumous-style rendering Emperor Wen.

decisions.reason: 詔令除討 says the late emperor ordered Lord Ling to suppress the Weizhou mutiny, not that he ordered Lord Ling punished.
父子之盟 explicitly denotes a father-and-son alliance, not brotherhood.

decisions.reason: The commander's name is 何福, He Fu; 賫 is the following verb meaning that he carried the memorial.

decisions.after: In the third month of the second year he ordered Xu Prefecture military governor Wang Yanchao and others to build fortifications at Li Yankou. They fought several thousand Khitan horsemen at Anping County and defeated them.
decisions.reason: 許州 is Xu Prefecture, not Xuzhou (徐州). The revision also removes closing Chinese editorial marks that were accidentally copied into the English sentence.
